$comment: Canonical per-game detection data for CameraUnlock head-tracking mods. This is the single source of truth for where each supported game lives on disk: env var name, Steam folder, GOG IDs, Epic/Xbox paths, executable relative path, Unity data folder (for Cecil patching), and the Microsoft Store package identity for UWP titles. Consumed by cameraunlock-core/powershell/GamePathDetection.psm1 and by lopari, whose catalog/mods.json per-mod `game` block is GENERATED from this file (lopari/scripts/sync-catalog-games.mjs) and must not be hand-edited. Mod-specific fields (which DLLs to deploy, mod version) do NOT belong here - those live in each mod's install.cmd CONFIG BLOCK and launcher-manifest.json. Adding a new game: pick a hyphen-lowercase id, fill in at minimum `display_name`, `env_var` and `executable_relpath`. `env_var` is omitted only for Microsoft Store packaged titles resolved by `msix_identity_name`, which are launched by package identity and have no install path to point an env var at. The per-game mod metadata (`loader`, `engine`, `repo`, `catalog_status`, `delivery_mode`) is optional and describes the head-tracking mod for that game: `loader` and `delivery_mode` are copied from the mod repo's launcher-manifest.json (`strategy` / `delivery_mode`), `repo` is the owner/name of that repo, `catalog_status` is released | prerelease | private | absent per lopari's catalog, and `engine` is the game's engine FAMILY (not version), populated only where it is mechanically verifiable and omitted otherwise. Any field that's empty for a given game should be omitted rather than set to a null/empty value.

Install xNVSE 6.4.1 or newer (github.com/xNVSE/NVSE/releases) into your game folder, then launch again. Strongly recommended: New Vegas Tick Fix / NVTF (nexusmods.com/newvegas/mods/66537) for smooth head-tracked camera motion.
